thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert triggered: AUTH_SIGNING_ERRORS spike (p50 5xx auth failures)

pagerduty: PagerDuty incident #PD-6291 created - Severity: P1 - Escalation: oncall-auth (page)

alec: acked. I'm on it. grabbing logs now.

mira: I can help with jwks and signing service. ping me @alec when you have the first reproduction.

alec: quick snapshot: increased 401s for token validation across hosted-api cluster-3 starting 2026-03-14T10:12Z. Error is "invalid_signature" from verifier. Root cause looks like kid mismatch on the tokens.

alec: past 5m sample from verifier logs: 
```
2026-03-14T10:12:04Z verifier-1 auth: token_id=abc123 client=webapp status=401 error="invalid_signature" token_kid="k9-2026-03-14" jwks_kids=["k8-2025-11-03","k7-2024-05-10"]
2026-03-14T10:12:09Z verifier-2 auth: token_id=def456 client=mobile status=401 error="no_matching_kid" token_kid="k9-2026-03-14" jwks_kids=["k8-2025-11-03","k7-2024-05-10"]
```

anya: that looks like the signing service started issuing tokens with kid=k9 but our JWKS endpoint hasn't published k9 yet.

jordan: confirm: did we rotate signing keys yesterday? I remember a deploy to signing-service around 03-13 23:xx UTC.

lee: yes, rollout of signing-service v2.4.1 included a new key generation path. There was a canary in staging but I didn't see any glogs about publish failure. Investigating the jwks publisher job.

mira: run this to check the JWKS endpoint from prod cluster-3: 
```
curl -sS https://auth.redwood-inference.com/.well-known/jwks.json | jq -c '.keys[].kid'
```

alec: output shows: "k8-2025-11-03","k7-2024-05-10" — no k9.

alec: tokens presented to verifier reference kid=k9. So signers and JWKS are out of sync. Likely publisher failed to upload to the bucket or cache invalidation problem.

pagerduty: oncall-auth escalation: page sent to infra lead @mira-2, then to security @anya-2 (mock escalation).

mira: I'm checking signing-service logs now. `kubectl -n auth logs deploy/signing-service --since=60m | grep publish_jwks` -> seeing errors: "failed to PUT jwks.json: AccessDenied" for the S3 bucket used by JWKS publisher.

jordan: S3 perms regression? Any IAM changes in the last 24h?

lee: we pushed an infra policy tweak to limit write access to the bucket earlier today as part of a cleanup. Might be blocking the new key upload. Rollback incoming?

alec: customer impact: hosted API tokens signed after 2026-03-14T09:50Z may fail to validate. Old tokens (issued before key rotate) are ok. Some dedicated customers who use hosted tokens for auth might see 401s on newly minted sessions. No data plane degradation.

anya: can we hotfix by having verifier fall back to local cache of signing keys for a short period? That would avoid immediate customer impact.

mira: verifier fallback exists but its cache TTL is short (60s). We can bump to 10m via feature flag. I'm preparing a canary rollout.

alec: plan (short): 1) bump verifier jwks-cache TTL to 10m (feature flag) 2) restart signing-service publisher with restored S3 perms so jwks.json contains k9 3) re-issue tokens for customers where session creation failed (ops script) 4) monitor 5xx/401 rates.

jordan: agree. I'll do (1) canary to 10% of prod verifiers now.

lee: I've reverted the IAM change that removed s3:PutObject for the jwks bucket — giving signing-service back write perms.

mira: attempted restart of signing-service publisher: logs now show successful PUT, returning 200. Confirmed jwks contains "k9-2026-03-14".

alec: verifier canary showed drop in invalid_signature errors within 90s after TTL bump. Rolling to 100% now.

anya: ops script to reissue tokens: 
```
python scripts/reissue_tokens.py --since 2026-03-14T09:50Z --env prod --dry-run
```

alec: dry-run shows ~420 tokens to reissue for third-party integrations. We'll coordinate reissuance with support.

jordan: handing off to mira — I need to jump to another pager after 10m. Mira, you're primary on-call now.

mira: taking over. I'll keep monitoring for 30m and then confirm stable.

lee: monitoring dashboards: auth 401 rate back to baseline ~2m after jwks PUT. No regressions in key publishing.

pagerduty: Incident PD-6291 status updated: acknowledged -> mitigated.

alec: customer impact note for status page: "Intermittent token validation failures for newly issued tokens between 2026-03-14T09:50Z and 2026-03-14T10:18Z due to JWKS publication error during key rotation. No data loss. Short-term mitigations applied. Engineers are working on hardening key publish flow."

anya: follow-ups (post-incident):
- Add end-to-end test for signing-service + jwks publication (CI)
- Add alert for unsuccessful S3 PUTs with 5m burn rate
- Document rollback steps for key rotation and add as runbook
- Increase default verifier jwks cache TTL during rotations to 5m

mira: I'll own the postmortem. Assigning action items in the incident tracker.

alec: final check: auth 401s stable for 15m, reissue queue started, support alerted to follow up with affected customers.

mira: closing out from on-call in 20m unless anything pops. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

alec: good job team. leaving notes for postmortem.

incident-bot: Incident PD-6291 auto-closed by system after 2h without new alerts.
